title: Application of UCP
summary: The Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits, 2007 Revision, ICC Publication No. 600 apply to any documentary credit when the text of the credit expressly indicates that it is subject to these rules. They are binding on all parties thereto unless expressly modified or excluded by the credit.
validation_rules: Credit must expressly state UCP 600 in :40E:
Any article may be modified or excluded by the credit — modifications are not violations but contractual choices
Exclusion of an article changes risk profile but does not render credit illegal
common_discrepancies: Credit refers to outdated UCP version (UCP 500)
:40E: absent or ambiguous
embedding_text: UCP 600 application scope credit expressly subject to rules binding parties modification exclusion article 1 ICC 2007 revision

title: Documents versus goods, services or performance
summary: Banks deal with documents and not with goods, services or performance to which the documents may relate. The terms and conditions of a credit — especially clauses in fields :47A: and :46A: — govern over SWIFT field tags when there is a contradiction. The documentary credit clause always prevails over tag defaults.
validation_rules: Banks examine documents on their face — underlying contract is irrelevant
When a textual clause in :47A: contradicts a SWIFT field tag, the clause prevails
Contradiction between :43T: and a no-transhipment clause must be resolved in favour of the clause
Banks bear no responsibility for genuineness, falsification or legal effect of documents
common_discrepancies: :43T: = ALLOWED but clause prohibits transhipment — clause prevails
SWIFT field states PERMITTED but additional condition text in :47A: restricts
Applicant assumes no liability is ignored — clause text governs

title: Availability, expiry date and place
summary: A credit must state the bank with which it is available, or whether it is available with any bank. A credit must state an expiry date for presentation. The place of the bank with which the credit is available is the place for presentation.
validation_rules: Expiry date must be present and in format YYMMDD
Place of expiry must be explicitly stated
Availability must specify BY PAYMENT, BY ACCEPTANCE, BY NEGOTIATION or BY DEF PAYMENT
If credit is available with any bank, expiry date governs presentation deadline
common_discrepancies: Expiry date missing or format invalid
Place of expiry not stated
Availability method not specified
embedding_text: Letter of credit expiry date place of presentation availability sight usance deferred payment acceptance negotiation UCP 600 article 6

title: Issuing bank undertaking
summary: An issuing bank is irrevocably bound to honour a complying presentation from the moment it issues the credit. An issuing bank undertakes to reimburse a nominated bank that has honoured or negotiated a complying presentation.
validation_rules: Credit must be irrevocable (field :40A: = IRREVOCABLE)
Issuing bank reimbursement obligation is unconditional for complying presentations
Undertaking is independent of underlying contract
common_discrepancies: Credit stated as revocable — not permitted under UCP 600
Reimbursement instructions absent in :78:
embedding_text: Issuing bank irrevocable undertaking honour reimburse nominated bank complying presentation documentary credit

title: Confirming bank undertaking
summary: A confirming bank is irrevocably bound to honour or negotiate a complying presentation from the moment it adds its confirmation. A confirming bank undertakes to reimburse another nominated bank that has honoured or negotiated a complying presentation.
validation_rules: Confirmation instructions field :49: must be CONFIRM, MAY ADD or WITHOUT
If CONFIRM, confirming bank bears same payment obligation as issuing bank
Confirmation cannot be added without issuing bank authorisation
common_discrepancies: Field :49: absent when confirming bank is designated
Silent confirmation not disclosed — creates undisclosed risk
embedding_text: Confirming bank confirmation undertaking honour negotiate reimburse letter of credit UCP 600 article 8

title: Advising of credits and amendments
summary: A credit and any amendment may be advised to a beneficiary through an advising bank. An advising bank that is not a confirming bank advises the credit and any amendment without any undertaking to honour or negotiate. An advising bank must verify the apparent authenticity of the credit it advises.
validation_rules: Advising bank must verify apparent authenticity of the credit
Advising bank has no payment obligation unless it also confirms
Amendment must be advised through same channel as original credit
Beneficiary acceptance of partial amendment not permitted
common_discrepancies: Authenticity of SWIFT message not verified
Amendment advised through different bank than original credit
Partial acceptance of amendment attempted
embedding_text: Advising bank credit amendment authenticity notification beneficiary letter of credit UCP 600 article 9

title: Amendments
summary: A credit can neither be amended nor cancelled without the agreement of the issuing bank, the confirming bank (if any), and the beneficiary. A beneficiary should give notification of acceptance or rejection of an amendment. An amendment cannot be accepted partially.
validation_rules: Amendment requires consent of issuing bank, confirming bank (if any) and beneficiary
Partial acceptance of amendment is NOT permitted
Silence does not constitute acceptance of amendment
Amendment cannot be unilaterally imposed by any party
Beneficiary can only reject amendment — cannot partially accept
common_discrepancies: Beneficiary attempts partial acceptance of amendment — invalid
Amendment clause allows tacit agreement — not permitted by UCP
Issuing bank amends without beneficiary consent
Multiple amendments create conflicting terms
embedding_text: Amendment modification credit requires consent issuing bank confirming beneficiary partial acceptance not permitted tacit agreement UCP 600 article 10 MT707

title: Designation and pre-payment restriction
summary: A nominated bank that pre-pays or purchases a draft accepted or a deferred payment undertaking incurred before the maturity date will be reimbursed on or after maturity. Article 12b excludes pre-payment by nominated bank without issuing bank authorisation.
validation_rules: Pre-payment before maturity requires explicit issuing bank authorisation
Art.12b exclusion means no pre-payment / discounting allowed
Nominated bank bears risk if it pre-pays without authorisation
common_discrepancies: Nominated bank discounts without authorisation — not reimbursable under UCP
Art.12b excluded — pre-payment requests must go to issuing bank

title: Standard for examination of documents
summary: Banks examine documents only against the credit terms and international standard banking practice. Documents must not conflict with each other. Data in a document need not be identical to, but must not conflict with, data in that document, any other stipulated document, the credit, or UCP 600.
validation_rules: Documents examined on their face only — underlying transaction irrelevant
Maximum 5 banking days to examine (Art.14b)
Data conflicts between documents constitute discrepancy
Documents not listed in credit may be disregarded (Art.14c)
Reference to ISBP 745 for interpretation of standard banking practice
common_discrepancies: Name/address conflict between invoice and transport document
Description of goods in invoice conflicts with :45A:
Currency mismatch between documents
Port of loading/discharge conflict between BL and LC terms

title: Five banking day rule for examination
summary: A nominated bank acting on its nomination, a confirming bank, if any, and the issuing bank shall each have a maximum of five banking days following the day of presentation to determine if a presentation is complying.
validation_rules: Maximum 5 banking days — not 5 calendar days
Period starts day after receipt of documents
Failure to act within 5 days precludes raising discrepancies
Banking days defined by place of examination, not beneficiary country
common_discrepancies: Bank examines beyond 5 banking days — precluded from claiming discrepancies
Refusal notice sent after deadline — bank must honour
Public holidays not correctly excluded from banking day count
embedding_text: Five banking days examination period complying presentation discrepancy notice UCP 600 article 14a deadline

title: Documents not required by the credit
summary: If a credit requires presentation of a document other than a transport document, insurance document or commercial invoice, without stipulating by whom the document is to be issued or its data content, banks will accept the document as presented if its content appears to fulfil the function of the required document.
validation_rules: Documents not called for by credit may be disregarded or returned without examination
Presenting unrequested documents creates no obligation on bank
Unstipulated issuer or data content — accept if function fulfilled
common_discrepancies: Beneficiary presents extra documents creating apparent conflicts — bank may disregard
embedding_text: Documents not called for by the letter of credit may be disregarded or returned without examination UCP 600 article 14c

title: Shipper on transport documents
summary: Any shipper or consignor name may appear on a transport document unless the credit stipulates otherwise. The shipper or consignor need not be the beneficiary of the credit.
validation_rules: Shipper name may differ from beneficiary unless credit restricts
Credit must explicitly state 'beneficiary as shipper' to restrict
Third party shipper acceptable by default
common_discrepancies: Credit restricts shipper to beneficiary but third party appears on BL — discrepancy
embedding_text: Shipper consignor name on bill of lading transport document unless credit requires beneficiary as shipper UCP 600 article 14k

title: Discrepant documents — waiver and notice
summary: When a nominated bank acting on its nomination, a confirming bank, or the issuing bank determines a presentation is not complying, it may refuse to honour or negotiate. When a bank decides to refuse, it must give a single notice to the presenter.
validation_rules: Single refusal notice required — multiple notices not permitted
Notice must list ALL discrepancies in one communication
Notice must state disposition of documents (hold / return / act on instructions)
Notice must be given within 5 banking days (Art.14a)
Failure to give proper notice precludes bank from claiming discrepancy
Bank may seek waiver from applicant but is not obligated to do so
common_discrepancies: Multiple refusal notices sent — precludes additional discrepancies
Disposition of documents not stated in notice
Notice given after 5 banking day deadline

title: Original documents and copies
summary: At least one original of each stipulated document is required. A bank treats as an original any document bearing an apparently original signature, mark, stamp, or label of the issuer, or purporting to be original. Scanned or photocopied documents are not originals.
validation_rules: Minimum one original per stipulated document required
Document marked 'original' qualifies even if produced by reprographic system
Document bearing original signature/stamp qualifies as original
Scanned documents are NEVER originals under UCP 600
Blue ink handwritten signature requirement if stipulated in :47A:
common_discrepancies: All copies presented, no original
Photocopy without original signature presented as original
Scanned document presented — never acceptable as original
Signature missing required blue ink if stipulated

title: Commercial invoice
summary: A commercial invoice must appear to have been issued by the beneficiary. It must be made out in the name of the applicant, and in the currency of the credit. The description of goods, services, or performance in a commercial invoice must correspond with that appearing in the credit.
validation_rules: Invoice must appear issued by beneficiary (matches :59:)
Invoice made out to applicant (matches :50:)
Description of goods must correspond exactly with :45A:
Currency must match :32B:
Invoice amount must not exceed credit amount (Art.18b)
Invoice need not be signed unless credit stipulates
Third party invoice: forbidden unless credit explicitly permits
'Formerly known as' wording on invoice creates identity discrepancy
common_discrepancies: Goods description on invoice does not match :45A:
Invoice issued in wrong currency
Invoice amount exceeds credit amount beyond tolerance
Invoice not issued in name of applicant
Beneficiary name on invoice differs from :59:
Third party invoice presented without authorisation
Invoice bears 'formerly known as' — name change not permitted
embedding_text: Commercial invoice issued by beneficiary matching letter of credit goods description applicant currency third party invoice prohibited name change UCP 600 article 18

title: Invoice amount and tolerance
summary: The amount of a commercial invoice must not exceed the amount permitted by the credit. However, if the credit states the quantity of goods and allows a tolerance in amount, the invoice amount may exceed the credit amount by that tolerance.
validation_rules: Invoice amount ≤ credit amount unless tolerance field (:39A:) is stated
:39A: format: percentage over/under (e.g., 05/05 = ±5%)
:39B: NOT EXCEEDING = no tolerance above credit amount
Cross-check with Art.30 quantity tolerance rules
Art.18b excluded = no 5% UCP tolerance — strict invoice amount
common_discrepancies: Invoice exceeds credit amount with no tolerance field
Tolerance percentage misread — 10/10 ≠ 10% over and 10% under
Art.18b excluded without informing beneficiary of strict limit
embedding_text: Commercial invoice amount must not exceed letter of credit amount tolerance field 39A 39B strict limit excluded UCP 600 article 18b

title: Bill of lading
summary: A bill of lading must indicate the name of the carrier and be signed by the carrier or a named agent, indicate that the goods have been shipped on board a named vessel at the port of loading stated in the credit, and indicate the port of loading and port of discharge stated in the credit. Blank back and short form BLs are prohibited.
validation_rules: Carrier name must appear and document signed by carrier or named agent
On-board notation required — pre-printed or added as notation with date
On-board date determines shipment date for latest shipment (:44C:)
Port of loading must match :44E: or :44A:
Port of discharge must match :44F: or :44B:
Full set = typically 3/3 originals unless credit states otherwise
Blank back BL is prohibited
LCL BL must not bear CY/CFS, LCL/FCL or CY/CFT
Additional notify party on BL is prohibited unless credit permits
common_discrepancies: On-board notation absent or undated
Port of loading/discharge does not match credit
Carrier not identified or agent unsigned without carrier name
Blank back or short form BL presented
On-board date later than latest shipment date :44C:
LCL BL bears forbidden mentions CY/CFS

title: Transhipment on bill of lading
summary: Transhipment means unloading from one vessel and reloading to another vessel during the carriage. A bill of lading indicating that transhipment will or may take place is acceptable, even if the credit prohibits transhipment, if the goods are shipped in a container, trailer or LASH barge. When the credit clause prohibits transhipment but SWIFT :43T: = ALLOWED, the clause prevails (Art.5).
validation_rules: Field :43T: must be ALLOWED or PROHIBITED
If PROHIBITED: BL must not indicate transhipment will occur
Exception: containerised cargo — transhipment acceptable even if prohibited
Entire carriage must be covered by one and the same BL
Clause prohibiting transhipment overrides :43T: = ALLOWED (Art.5 UCP)
common_discrepancies: BL shows transhipment when :43T: = PROHIBITED and cargo not containerised
Two separate BLs presented instead of single through BL
CONTRADICTION: clause prohibits transhipment but :43T: = ALLOWED
embedding_text: Transhipment allowed prohibited containerised transport clause overrides SWIFT tag 43T UCP 600 article 20c article 5

title: Insurance document and coverage
summary: An insurance document must indicate the name of the insurer or their agent, be signed by the insurer or their agent, cover the risks specified in the credit, and be for a minimum amount of 110% of CIF or CIP value. No franchise or excess deductible is acceptable. Warranted clauses and coverage restrictions are prohibited.
validation_rules: Minimum coverage: 110% of CIF or CIP invoice value
Insurance currency must match credit currency (:32B:)
Risks must be those specified in :46A: (ICC-A, ICC-B, ICC-C, or named risks)
Insurance document date ≤ on-board date on BL (cover from point of shipment)
Open cover / certificate acceptable if issued by insurer or agent
Franchise and excess deductible are PROHIBITED
Warranted clauses ('warranted professionally packed') are PROHIBITED
Coverage restriction clauses (Institute Cargo Clauses limitation) PROHIBITED
common_discrepancies: Coverage amount less than 110% of invoice
Insurance currency differs from credit currency
Insurance date later than shipment date — gap in coverage
Wrong ICC clause (e.g., ICC-C when ICC-A stipulated)
Broker's cover note presented — not acceptable
Franchise or deductible present on policy

title: Extension of expiry date or last day for presentation
summary: If the expiry date or the last day for presentation falls on a day when the bank to which presentation is to be made is closed, the expiry date or the last day for presentation will be extended to the first following banking day.
validation_rules: Automatic extension applies when expiry falls on non-banking day
Extension to first following banking day only
On-board notation date is not extended — shipment deadline is separate
Article 36 force majeure events do NOT trigger Art.29 extension
common_discrepancies: Presentation made on first extended banking day but shipment date also adjusted — invalid
Bank closed for reasons other than public holiday — confirm banking day status
embedding_text: Extension expiry date last day presentation banking day closed letter of credit UCP 600 article 29

title: Tolerance in credit amount, quantity and unit prices
summary: The words 'about' or 'approximately' used in connection with the amount, quantity or unit price allow a tolerance not to exceed 10%. A tolerance not to exceed 5% more or 5% less in the quantity of goods is allowed, unless the credit stipulates the quantity in terms of a stipulated number of packing units.
validation_rules: 'About'/'approximately' in amount → ±10% tolerance on amount AND unit price
Default quantity tolerance ±5% if not in packing units/individual items
No default tolerance if quantity expressed as number of units/items
Partial drawings must remain within :39A: tolerance bands
Invoice amount may be less than credit amount — not a discrepancy
common_discrepancies: Invoice 6% over credit amount with no :39A: tolerance field
'About USD 100,000' — tolerance applies to amount, not just quantity
Quantity 7% over when stipulated in 'cartons' — no tolerance applies

title: Partial drawings and partial shipments
summary: Partial drawings or presentations are allowed. Partial shipments are allowed. Presentations made or dispatched on the same means of conveyance and for the same journey, even if different bills of lading indicate different dates, will not be regarded as partial shipments.
validation_rules: Default: partial shipments ALLOWED unless :43P: = PROHIBITED
Same vessel / same voyage / different BL dates — NOT partial shipment
Multiple presentations on same day under same credit — partial drawing
Each partial drawing reduces available credit amount
common_discrepancies: Multiple BLs on same vessel treated as partial shipment — incorrect
Second drawing exceeds remaining balance after first partial drawing
:43P: = PROHIBITED but multiple BLs presented

title: Instalment drawings and shipments
summary: If a credit calls for drawings or shipments in instalments within given periods and any instalment is not drawn or shipped within the period allowed for that instalment, the credit ceases to be available for that and any subsequent instalment, unless the credit stipulates otherwise.
validation_rules: Missing one instalment period causes all subsequent instalments to lapse automatically
No automatic reinstatement — credit terminates for future instalments
Instalment schedule must be explicitly defined in credit
Different from partial shipments — instalment credits have defined periodic windows
common_discrepancies: Instalment missed — subsequent drawings refused even if credit still valid
Instalment schedule ambiguous — advising bank must seek clarification

title: Hours of presentation
summary: A bank has no obligation to accept a presentation outside of its banking hours. A document may be presented any time before the expiry date, but the bank's counter hours govern acceptance on the day of presentation.
validation_rules: Presentation must be within banking hours on the expiry date
Credit may specify a time (e.g., 'before 5 PM local time')
If no time specified, bank's standard counter hours apply
common_discrepancies: Documents submitted after banking hours on expiry date — not accepted

title: Disclaimer on transmission and translation
summary: A bank assumes no liability or responsibility for the consequences arising out of delay, loss in transit, mutilation or other errors arising in the transmission of any messages or delivery of letters or documents. A bank assumes no liability for errors in translation.
validation_rules: Banks not liable for SWIFT transmission errors or message corruption
Translation errors in documents — bank not liable
Bank not responsible for delays caused by external communication systems
common_discrepancies: Beneficiary claims discrepancy arose from transmission error — bank not liable

title: Bank charges and commissions
summary: If a credit states that charges are for the account of the beneficiary, and the charges cannot be collected, the issuing bank remains liable. Article 37c exclusion means all charges outside the issuing country fall on the beneficiary.
validation_rules: If :71B: = ALL CHARGES FOR BENEFICIARY, all bank fees are deducted from payment
Art.37c exclusion: charges cannot be waived back to applicant
Reservation lifting fees, SWIFT charges and commissions all apply
Inform beneficiary of all applicable charges before presentation
common_discrepancies: Beneficiary unaware of charges — payment net of charges creates shortfall
Art.37c excluded but charges still taken — contra-contractual

title: Transferable credits
summary: A credit can be transferred only if it is expressly designated as 'transferable' by the issuing bank. A transferable credit may be made available in whole or in part to another beneficiary (second beneficiary). Transfer is possible only on the terms and conditions specified in the original credit, with specified exceptions.
validation_rules: Credit must be expressly marked 'TRANSFERABLE' — not implied
Only first beneficiary may request transfer
Transfer to second beneficiary: amount may be reduced, unit price reduced, expiry earlier, shipment earlier, presentation shorter
Re-transfer to original beneficiary not permitted
Transferable does not mean back-to-back — different legal mechanism
common_discrepancies: Transfer requested when credit not designated transferable
Second beneficiary attempts to re-transfer — not permitted
Transferred credit amount exceeds original — invalid

title: Substitution of invoices in transferable credits
summary: The first beneficiary has the right to substitute its own invoices and drafts for those of a second beneficiary. On substitution, the first beneficiary can draw under the credit for the difference between its own invoice amount and the second beneficiary's invoice amount.
validation_rules: First beneficiary's substituted invoice must not exceed original credit amount
Substituted invoice must match goods description in credit (Art.18)
If first beneficiary fails to substitute, transferring bank may present second beneficiary's docs
Drafts substitution follows same rules as invoice substitution
Art.38i exclusion: invoices MUST be from first beneficiary only — no substitution rights
common_discrepancies: Substituted invoice amount exceeds original credit amount
Substituted invoice description conflicts with :45A:
First beneficiary fails to substitute within presentation period

title: Assignment of proceeds
summary: The fact that a credit is not stated to be transferable shall not affect the right of the beneficiary to assign any proceeds to which it may be or may become entitled under the credit, in accordance with the provisions of applicable law. This article relates only to the assignment of proceeds and not to the assignment of the right to perform under the credit.
validation_rules: Assignment of proceeds does not require credit to be transferable
Assignment is of payment entitlement only — not of right to perform
Bank must be formally notified of any assignment
Assignment prohibited by clause = contractual restriction (Art.1 UCP)
common_discrepancies: Beneficiary assigns proceeds without notifying bank
Credit prohibits assignment — beneficiary proceeds despite restriction
Assignment confused with transfer — different legal right
